subject: PillarPay service degradation — unified fallback summary & customer update
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T02:12:00Z
Subject: [SEV2] PillarPay: model errors rising on payments route (initial bridge)

Team — jumping on the bridge (PD INC-98231). Since ~01:45 UTC we've seen an uptick of 502s and model stacktrace errors for requests routed to rwd-13b/quant. Error rate ~8% of requests on /v1/generate for PillarPay production.

What we've done so far:
- Isolated a subset of offending requests (long sequences + embedded JSON payloads)
- Disabled the latest kernel optimization flag on a small cohort
- Launched a short-term traffic split to rwd-13b/float for two hosts

Ask: can we consider an automated unified fallback to rwd-7b-q4f for latency-preserving degraded mode? That will reduce token cost and should keep 99th latency within SLO while we debug quant path. If agreed, I can coordinate the rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%) and update the customer.

Attaching a 1-page bridge-log-brief with sample traces and the most common stackframes.

Attachment: bridge-log-brief.pdf (1 page)

—Dylan
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pillarpay.com>, Nicole Huang <nicole@pillarpay.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T03:00:00Z
Subject: PillarPay — executive status update (interim)

Alex, Nicole —

Thanks for your patience this morning. I’m Soojin Lee (Head of Customer Reliability). Quick summary of where we are and our plan:

- Impact: Some production generate requests to PillarPay’s payments flow are returning errors (manifesting as 502s and model execution faults). We estimate ~8% of requests over the last 30m were affected.
- Immediate relief: Our ops team has pushed traffic to a compatible model variant and disabled a recent kernel optimization on a portion of fleet. We are proposing a unified fallback to a smaller, quantized-compatible model to restore full capacity while preserving responsiveness.
- Next steps (next 90 minutes):
  1) Approve unified fallback to rwd-7b-q4f (canary -> 25% -> 100%) so we can stop user-facing errors.
  2) We will continue root cause analysis (telemetry shows failure in quantized attention kernel when payloads include long JSON arrays).
  3) We will follow up with a full timeline and postmortem draft by EOD today and a public postmortem within 48 hours.

If you approve the fallback, we’ll proceed and confirm when the canary is healthy. If you prefer a different course, let us know immediately.

We’ll update you with a concrete remediation ETA within the hour.

— Soojin
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pillarpay.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: platform@pillarpay.com
Date: 2027-03-21T03:12:00Z
Subject: Re: PillarPay — executive status update (interim)

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the rapid response. Can you confirm whether requests that fail are only those with batched payment payloads (we send arrays of up to 150 items), or is this affecting single-item flows too? Also, will the fallback change inference output enough to require us to re-validate signatures on our end?

If fallback is safe for outputs (no semantic changes to the expected labels), we’re OK to proceed; we just need confirmation that the canonical response fields are stable.

— Alex
VP Product, PillarPay
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T03:40:00Z
Subject: Re: PillarPay — unified fallback proposal

Soojin — short technical note for the customer reply:

- Root cause hypothesis: quantized attention kernel regressed on certain input shapes (long arrays + many numeric tokens) after the 2027-03-18 kernel shuffle. Single-item flows are mostly unaffected; batched arrays > 64 items show the highest error rate.
- Fallback impact: rwd-7b-q4f preserves the same response schema; we don’t change fingerprinting/signature fields. There is a measurable delta in probs but not in canonical labels for our verification tests.
- Rollout plan: do canary on 3 hosts (5% traffic) for 10 minutes, validate error rate and 99th latency; escalate to 25% then 100% if healthy.

I’ll run the canary now unless you want to hold. Attachment: unified-fallback-playbook.md (playbook + verification checks).

—Ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pillarpay.com>, Nicole Huang <nicole@pillarpay.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T06:30:00Z
Subject: PillarPay — remediation in place and follow-up plan

Alex / Nicole —

Update: we completed the canary and validated the fallback verification suite. We rolled the unified fallback to 25% at 04:10 UTC and to 100% at 05:05 UTC. Error rates have dropped to <0.1% across the payments route and 99th latency is within SLO.

What this means for you today:
- Normalized behavior: The payments flow should be restored for all users. You should no longer see 502s from our side.
- Output stability: We verified canonical fields used by your downstream signature validation remain unchanged. There is a small probability of probability-score deltas; we will document the test vectors we ran in the postmortem.
- Next commits: Internal RCA and postmortem draft (incl. mitigation & long-term fix) by EOD 21 Mar. Public postmortem and timeline for kernel fix within 48 hours.

Attachments: postmortem-outline.docx (high-level timeline + owners).

If you notice any residual issues, please reply and we’ll prioritize. Thank you for working with us through the bridge — we know this impacts your users and appreciate the rapid coordination.

— Soojin
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-bridge next steps and owners (internal)

Nice job getting remediation in. Quick internal follow-up:

- Postmortem draft (owner: Marissa) — due 2027-03-21 18:00 UTC. Include sample failing traces, telemetry, and customer-facing summary.
- Kernel rollback plan (owner: Karthik) — provide schedule for a targeted rollback or patch and estimated regression window.
- Customer QA deck (owner: Ben) — include the verification vectors we used and a short note about why canonical fields are stable.
- Billing/credits review (owner: Soojin + Sales) — evaluate goodwill credit given user impact window.

I’ll start the postmortem skeleton and share a Drive link. Team, flag any blockers now.

— Marissa
Senior Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference
